Event/Bulletin Title: Massachusetts Level 3 Critical Drought – WarRoom Empty and Not Listed After 3 Hours (Danaher)
Automation Opportunity: Monitoring that a WarRoom becomes visible and populated within an agreed window of the notification being sent, with alerting when it does not
Comments: From Jira CAN-3278 (Closed). Danaher received the notification email for the Massachusetts Level 3 Critical Drought WarRoom, but the WarRoom was empty across Suppliers, Sites, Parts and Products and was absent from the WarRoom listing page more than three hours after creation. CS recorded it as reproducible and as a likely regression of CAN-2921. Cause established by Engineering as a production defect in Resilinc Analytics, fixed and verified in late March, and conveyed to the customer.
RCA Details: Production fault in Resilinc Analytics, established on the ticket by Engineering (Sagar Date). Two faults sat in the same window. First, Customer Impact notifications were failing in production and analysts were manually re-triggering the affected events; twelve events over the preceding month were affected, including 'Authorities Declare Level 3 Critical Drought for Parts of Massachusetts, USA', the event behind this record. That fix was deployed to production on 21-Mar-2026 with no recurrence since. Second, the API that asynchronously populates event site summary data was sitting in its queue for over five hours because the required configuration was missing and the service fell back to a default queue size of 8; the execution pool was raised to a core size of 16, a maximum of 50 and a queue capacity of 2000, and database connections from 16 initial to 48 maximum. Those configurations were deployed on 27-Mar-2026, the what-if event flow was re-verified with Rohit Sawant on 31-Mar-2026, and backend checks confirmed event data being created in near real time. This was not an EventWatch analyst or process failure: the cause was an engineering configuration and notification defect, which is why the record routes to Product & Platform.

Event/Bulletin Title: Fire at FXI Foam Manufacturing Plant in Cuautitlan, Mexico
Automation Opportunity: Relevance scoring that stops treating supplier mapping as a dominant decision factor for major industrial incidents, weighting incident severity, manufacturing activity, facility type, industry relevance and downstream supply chain potential instead, so an unmapped manufacturing site is not closed out before an analyst has weighed it
Comments: Customer reported a fire at FXI, a Tier 2 supplier, causing a Force Majeure at Sage Automotive Interiors, with no matching EventWatch notification. Established as a relevance-scoring weakness rather than an analyst error: the event was captured, classified Not Impactful because the company was unmapped, and the analyst review concurred. Resilinc accepted the customer's challenge to the methodology, issued an ICA on 17-Jul-2026 adding a manual review for major industrial incidents initially classified Not Impactful, and committed to a PCA enhancing the AI relevance-scoring models by end July 2026.
RCA Details: A methodology weakness that Resilinc accepted, not an analyst error. EventWatch did capture multiple public reports of the 28-Jun-2026 fire at the foam manufacturing facility in Cuautitlan Izcalli, Mexico. The AI classification models then categorised it Not Impactful on three grounds: the company was not a mapped supplier in the database, no mapped supplier sites sat near the incident, and public reporting described a mattress/foam plant fire with no confirmed downstream impact. The reporting team reviewed the captured articles under human-in-the-loop validation and concurred, so nothing was published. The Force Majeure that Sage Automotive Interiors issued could not be confirmed in English or Spanish public sources and appears to have gone through direct supplier channels, so EventWatch could not publish it either; a monitoring record was created to catch any public confirmation. The customer challenged the methodology itself - why supplier presence in an internal database filters an assessment that is meant to rest on public information - and Resilinc agreed the observation was right. Interim corrective action, in force now: major industrial incidents at manufacturing facilities initially classified Not Impactful get an additional manual review, and are no longer closed solely on the absence of mapped suppliers or immediately confirmed downstream impact; analysts weigh facility type, manufacturing activity, incident severity, industry relevance and downstream potential before the publication decision. Permanent corrective action: the AI relevance-scoring models are being enhanced so supplier mapping is no longer a dominant factor, shared with Data Science and on the AI roadmap, targeted for deployment by end July 2026, at which point the interim manual control folds into the automated decision.

Event/Bulletin Title: Typhoon Dolphin Bulletins Distributed Across Two WarRooms
Automation Opportunity: Make the shared update sequence legible on the bulletin itself, so a jump from Update 2 to Update 5 in one country's WarRoom shows which storm-lifecycle updates ran under the other WarRooms instead of reading as missing bulletins
Comments: EAO-29: Bulletins were distributed across two WarRooms, resulting in gaps in the update sequence. Customer requested RCA; RCA shared.
RCA Details: Not duplicate WarRooms and not a defect: a question about a deliberate internal convention. Country-specific WarRooms for one storm share a single update sequence so the chronology of the underlying event stays end to end. A storm evolves over days, changes direction and intensity and crosses borders, and a shared sequence lets a customer exposed in several geographies see where each development sits in the overall lifecycle. It also signals maturity of the threat: restarting the numbering for each new country would make an established, highly disruptive typhoon appear as an Initial Bulletin. It further preserves cross-country traceability, since independent numbering would produce several Update 1s and Update 2s for the same storm. The WarRoom says where a development is relevant; the update number says where it falls in the storm's lifecycle. So when the China WarRoom runs from Update 2 to Update 5, Updates 3 and 4 are not missing - they were intervening Typhoon Dolphin developments relevant to Japan and published under the Japan WarRoom, the same principle covering Update 7 for Taiwan. The explanation was shared with the customer, who was invited to give further feedback.

Automation Opportunity: Reconciliation between what the vendor feeds deliver and what actually reaches the analyst portal, so a harvested item that never surfaces is caught rather than found by a customer; plus an evidence grade carried on the event itself - confirmed, credible but unconfirmed, disputed, unsubstantiated, demonstrably false - so a customer can see the basis of a report without asking, and name-collision detection on the mapping surface so a near-identical supplier name is flagged at mapping time
Comments: EAO-39: Belden asked why they received no EventWatch notification and saw no related news for TSMC's 28nm production capacity reduction. The query ran on through two follow-ups, both part of the same contact rather than separate records. First, on 18-Sep-2026 the customer cited a 22-Jun-2026 report that TSMC denied phasing out 28nm and asked how EventWatch separates real reporting from fake, what criteria establish that a notification is not fake, and whether the 28nm reduction is real; a written assessment was issued covering the source hierarchy, the five evidence grades and the TSMC timeline. Second, on 22-Sep-2026 the customer corrected their own position and confirmed TSMC is not mapped in their BOM - they source the wafer via Broadcom, and the Taiwan Semiconductor entity they had mapped covers resistors and MOSFETs - so no customer notification was owed. Reclassified on review from Complaint to Inquiry with Missed_Flag No, and logged under Source Coverage.
RCA Details: Not a source-coverage gap in the ingestion sense. The news was captured by the vendor sources but never surfaced on the analyst portal, so it was never available for review and no coverage was created; the failure sits between ingestion and the analyst queue. The customer's exposure claim did not hold either: Belden confirmed on 22-Sep-2026 that TSMC is not mapped in their BOM, having mapped Taiwan Semiconductor Co., Ltd. (resistors and MOSFETs) rather than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. The two are different suppliers in different commodities and the near-identical name is what led the customer to expect coverage; nothing in the mapping surface flags that collision. On the authenticity question the report was assessed as credible but unconfirmed public reporting of a selective production and capacity shift at Fab 15A: Commercial Times (22-Jun-2026) reported monthly 28nm wafer starts falling from roughly 200,000 to 150,000 with migration toward 12nm and reallocation to silicon-interposer production, Economic Daily News (May 2026) reported Fab 15A converting toward 4nm, and TrendForce, SemiMedia, Tech in Asia and GuruFocus carried or analysed the same upstream reporting. TSMC stated on 22-Jun-2026 that its overall mature-node strategy was unchanged, which is not contradictory - an unchanged strategy is compatible with selective conversion at one fab. The specific 25 percent reduction came from supply-chain sources and was never confirmed by TSMC, so it is not classified as fake.

Event/Bulletin Title: Clarification on Impact Confirmation Requests for Supplier Acquisitions (Eaton)
Automation Opportunity: Publish the M&A impact-confirmation trigger criteria in-product, so the rationale for an acquiring-side outreach is visible on the request itself instead of being explained per account after the fact
Comments: Staged from Jira EAO-43 (In Progress). Eaton asked why Supplier Impact Confirmation requests are issued to a Tier-1 supplier when that supplier is the acquiring party, as distinct from a merger or business sale where integration impact is understandable. Three questions: what specific risks or impacts the notification assesses, which supply chain disruption scenarios are commonly associated with acquisitions, and what criteria Resilinc uses to decide an acquisition event warrants supplier outreach. No event or WarRoom was named and no service failure is alleged. Follows EAO-38, the same account's query on the Vertiv acquisition. A written explanation was issued on 23-Sep-2026.
RCA Details: Not a defect. Under the updated EventWatch Supplier Impact Confirmation methodology the outreach criteria were widened across event types in response to customer requests for greater visibility. For a Merger & Acquisition the confirmation request validates whether the transaction has created operational or supply-chain impact that is not yet publicly known; a 'no impact' reply is itself useful because it confirms continuity of supply, and disruption is not assumed. The trigger ladder given to the customer: Low, neither company mapped and the transaction is an informational industry development, so no confirmation is sent; Medium, a mapped Tier-1 acquires a non-mapped company with no confirmed disruption, so outreach may be initiated to validate impact; High, a mapped company or site has confirmed operational or supply-chain disruption. Where the company being acquired or sold is itself mapped, the event is handled under Business Sale criteria.

Event/Bulletin Title: UPG Enterprises Chapter 11 Mapped to Mapes & Sprowl - Mapping and Severity Queried (Eaton)
Automation Opportunity: Scope check on parent-subsidiary linkage for insolvency filings, so a WarRoom is not raised against a subsidiary the filing text explicitly excludes, plus a recorded basis for the severity grade

RCA Details: Deliberate precautionary scoping, explained to the customer on 24-Sep-2026. Mapes & Sprowl is an affiliate operating within the UPG family of companies, and the official press release stated that UPG Enterprises LLC filed for Chapter 11 together with certain of its affiliates. That announcement did name UPG's international operations and UPG Electrical and its subsidiaries as outside the filing, but Mapes & Sprowl was not among the entities explicitly excluded. Given the complex corporate hierarchies typical of industrial holding groups and the broad umbrella language of the initial disclosure, connected entities were included in the WarRoom as a precautionary early-warning measure to minimise visibility gaps. Inclusion was not a statement that Mapes & Sprowl had itself filed: the WarRoom gives supply chain and procurement teams a workspace to begin supplier outreach, establish which operating entities fall inside the filing scope, and assess upstream or downstream impact from the parent's restructuring. On severity, the Bankruptcy-specific reporting guideline in the EventWatch Thresholds and Guidelines states that a mapped company is reported with High severity, and Mapes & Sprowl was identified as mapped during the initial assessment, so High followed from that rule.
